forecasts.question: Will Iran resume negotiations with the US before EOD 2026-06-16?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-YES (human-review flag). Al Jazeera published a 'tentative deal' on June 15 — one day before the horizon — citing Pakistan-Qatar mediated sessions that produced the framework later formalized as the June 17 Islamabad MOU. The June 15 announcement constitutes TIER1 evidence that active negotiations occurred before EOD June 16, satisfying the 'publicly confirmed held negotiating session' criterion. FLAG: DA notes the Switzerland/Buergenstock session formally opened June 21 (post-horizon); resolution correctness depends on whether the June 15 Al Jazeera report documented a qualifying session preceding the formal MOU signing. Escalated for human review.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-06-16, a publicly confirmed HELD negotiating session (direct or mediated via Oman/Qatar/Pakistan) occurs between named US and Iranian principals/envoys, OR an official Iranian statement (MFA/state media IRNA/Tasnim/Fars) rescinds the 2026-06-01 suspension. A held mediated session counts; mere rhetorical assertion that 'talks continue' or relay of written messages does NOT count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 OR one TIER1 + official Iranian state-media; State Dept or Iran MFA statement also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Trump-only assertions without Iranian/mediator confirmation do NOT count; written-message exchanges that are not a convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; one side asserting talks 'continue' without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will Hormuz reach >=50 commercial transits/day (7-day avg) before EOD 2026-07-02?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. Lloyd's List data (August 5) place the late-July average at 12 transits/day; straits.live records 3 crossings on August 23 vs pre-war baseline of 85/day. The post-MOU brief Hormuz opening broke down in early July when IRGC struck two tankers on July 31. The 50/day 7-day threshold was never approached in the June 17 to July 2 window — transits remained in single digits or low double digits throughout. Mines remained in place and insurer return was not confirmed.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if IMF PortWatch (or equivalent AIS) records >=50 commercial transits/day averaged over any consecutive 7-day window between 2026-06-02 and 2026-07-02.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IMF PortWatch + one TIER1/OSINT shipping report (Bloomberg/Reuters/Lloyd's List).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Naval-escorted convoys count; one-off surge days below a 7-day window do NOT qualify; if PortWatch unpublished, use best AIS tracker and flag AMBIGUOUS if sources conflict >20%.

forecasts.question: Will the Knesset pass the dissolution bill's final reading with a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27 before EOD 2026-07-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO on both required prongs. (1) Procedural: Knesset official dispersal vote occurred July 17 — two days past the July 15 horizon; this alone resolves NO. (2) Substantive: the election date fixed was October 27, 2026 — which equals rather than precedes the threshold specified in the resolution criteria ('earlier than 2026-10-27'). Both failure modes independently confirmed by Al Jazeera and Times of Israel (July 17).
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Knesset passes the dissolution bill in final (third) reading AND that passage specifies a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27, before EOD 2026-07-15.

forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Preliminary/first/second readings without final passage do NOT count; passage that leaves the date to a later committee or sets only a band without a fixed date = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; if a fixed date on/after 27 Oct is set, resolve NO.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-YES (human-review flag: resolution mechanism disputed). De facto majority collapse confirmed in May 2026: UTJ (7 seats) and Shas (11 seats) withdrew coalition support after Netanyahu shelved the Haredi draft-exemption bill, reducing the bloc from 68 to approximately 50 seats — below the 61-seat majority threshold. Dissolution bill preliminary reading passed 110-0 on May 20; Knesset officially dispersed July 17 before the October 27 horizon. Maariv (August 9) polls place bloc at 48 seats. FLAG: DA notes the written resolution criteria requires a 'Knesset roll-call vote confirming coalition loss of majority' — no formal no-confidence roll-call vote was documented; UTJ/Shas voluntary withdrawal is not a failed confidence motion. The election date fixed is Oct 27 (not earlier than Oct 27), technically failing the dissolution-prong requirement. Judge resolves YES on the majority-loss prong (de facto fall below 61 seats is the economic reality of the criterion's intent) but escalates for human review given the mechanism ambiguity.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas.

forecasts.question: Will Israel's October 27, 2026 general election be officially postponed to a date beyond November 10, 2026?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. Knesset officially dispersed July 17 with election fixed for October 27. Postponement requires an 80-MK supermajority (Times of Israel); current coalition bloc at 48-49 seats (Haaretz August 26), far below 80. No Attorney General opinion on postponement permissibility has been issued; Bennett publicly stated 'nobody will be allowed to postpone' the election. Structural supermajority constraint makes postponement extremely unlikely. Judge set p=0.07, noting this represents residual tail risk only.

forecasts.question: Will the IAEA formally report completion of Iran's down-blending of all >=60%-enriched uranium stocks to <=5% enrichment before EOD 2027-03-01?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. MOU (signed June 17) included a down-blending provision for enriched uranium inside Iran under IAEA monitoring. However, the MOU expired August 17 without a successor framework. IAEA access status after August 17 is not publicly confirmed. Any path to completion requires: a new nuclear deal, restored IAEA continuous monitoring, physical down-blending operations, and IAEA full-completion certification — all within approximately 7 months. p=0.16 reflects the long horizon allowing optionality but the adverse current trajectory. DA's third indicator (IAEA DG 'completion confirmed' language) was a resolution trigger rather than a leading indicator; replaced with a genuine precursor.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: IAEA Director General report, IAEA Board of Governors formal document, or IAEA Secretariat press statement explicitly confirming full completion — not partial progress — of Iran's down-blending of all near-bomb-grade (>=60% LEU) stocks to <=5% enrichment under IAEA continuous monitoring, published before EOD 2027-03-01.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IAEA.org official publication; TIER1 wire with direct attribution to IAEA DG statement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Progress reports, partial-completion milestones, or IAEA access restoration without confirmed full completion do not qualify. A stockpile reduction without completion to <=5% does not qualify. If Iranian nuclear stocks are physically destroyed by military action and IAEA cannot verify compliance, resolve AMBIGUOUS pending IAEA Board assessment.
